notes.text:
Relative to the ENTIRE qualified G331 only, this note reconstructs the canonical envelope and the dimension-two normal result used below. Current416 and current413 notes, source ledgers, programs, verdicts and compiler records are DATA, not accepted supports. Every G331 annotation remains binding: its core consists of actual negative effective finite REAL Cartier presentations on directed ACTUAL primary blowups, with nonnegative degree on EVERY contracted proper integral curve; its C and D are the uniform and actual decreasing-net completions. Its comparison with ideal classes and full-fibre positive descent are granted. Arbitrary birational-model cofinality, envelopes and characteristic-free resolution are not granted.

Let R be excellent reduced local, a proper primary gauge, and X=V_a(R), retaining EVERY prime support. For finite continuous signed f put A_0=R and A_m={g in R: v(g)+m f(v)>=0 for every v in X}. If M=max(0,-min f), then a^N is contained in A_m for N>=mM, N>0. Addition, scalar multiplication and the ultrametric inequality prove idealness. A negative value of f excludes every unit, making A_m proper primary; if f>=0, A_m=R. Multiplication gives A_m A_n subset A_(m+n). A monic ideal-integrality equation proves A_m integrally closed by the unique least-valued leading-term argument, including infinite values by treating them separately. The profile h_m=-v(A_m)/m is continuous and below f. Its divisor -E_(A_m)/m on Bl_(A_m)(R) is ACTUAL negative effective Cartier and relatively ample. Its restriction to every contracted integral curve is ample, hence has positive degree. The unit case is zero. Thus the approximants have independently geometric positivity before their limit is identified.

The raw pointwise supremum p(f)=sup{u in D:u<=f} equals the supremum over C, the supremum of rational primary/unit competitors, and sup_m h_m. Indeed a rational competitor -v(I)/r has I subset A_r. Uniform rational approximation of any C competitor, followed by a small negative rational gauge constant (ideal multiplication after common denominators), yields rational competitors converging from below. If u=inf_i g_i<=f is an actual decreasing C-net, the open sets {g_i<f+epsilon} cover compact X and increase under directed refinement. A finite subcover and one common index give g_i-epsilon<=f everywhere and u<=p_C(f)+epsilon. This also covers bottom and partial poles. No positivity of a raw supremum is assumed.

Put M_1=||v(A_1)|| and H_N=max_(1<=r<=N) h_r. For m=kr+s, 0<=s<r, grading gives h_m>=(kr/m)h_r-sM_1/m>=h_r-rM_1/m. Therefore H_N-NM_1/m<=h_m<=p. All degrees converge pointwise to a finite nonpositive lower semicontinuous p. Continuity of p is equivalent to uniform convergence of H_N, and to uniform convergence of h_m: if p is continuous, the increasing open sets {H_N>p-epsilon} cover compact X; the displayed bound then controls every sufficiently large degree. Conversely a uniform limit of h_m is continuous and belongs to closed geometric C. In this case p is the greatest C/D minorant. Subtracting an epsilon gauge constant from a D competitor proves ||p(f)-p(g)||<=||f-g||. A finite homogeneous generating set for the canonical algebra would make p the rational profile -v((g_i^(L/d_i)))/L, for L divisible by all generator degrees d_i; evaluate homogeneous expressions and pure powers. This elementary forward implication needs no section-algebra finite-generation theorem.

Primary change b is exact: d(v)=v(b)>0, T(v)=v/d(v), and f_b(Tv)=f_a(v)/d(v). Every defining inequality divides by d, so ALL A_m are unchanged and profiles/envelopes divide by d. Both d and 1/d are bounded. G331's completion homeomorphism and exact primary contraction transport the canonical ideals and profiles. If f_i decrease through continuous obstacles with C envelopes, inf_i p(f_i) is an actual decreasing C-net and is the greatest D minorant of inf_i f_i, since every competitor is below each p(f_i).

Here is the repaired dimension-two normal proof, without importing the current416 verdict. For an excellent normal local DOMAIN R of dimension TWO, dominate any finite primary-ideal list INCLUDING a by its product blowup and finite normalization. Its punctured base is regular, and the normal projective surface has finitely many singular points: excellence gives an open regular locus and normality excludes codimension-one singularities. Their local completions are normal by excellence. These verify EXACTLY condition (4) in Stacks54.14.5. The complete immediate proof, with54.14.3--4, resolves this surface by finitely many normalized blowups over its singular closed points. Deeper complete-normal-surface resolution, rational/double-point reduction, completion transfer and gluing remain the disclosed published foundations; they are not a fresh recursive audit or a higher-dimensional resolution premise.

The resulting regular Y is projective and unchanged off the marked point. Pullback of the initial negative tautological bundle is ample under finite normalization; the successive negative tautological bundles and sufficiently large pullback powers combine by Stacks29.38.7--8 into O(-E), where E is effective exceptional integral with full support. The initial primary divisor ensures positivity at EVERY exceptional prime. Stacks37.53.6 gives H^0(Y,O)=R: Y is integral proper birational over normal R and its generic fibre has sections Frac(R).

Y is an ACTUAL primary blowup, as follows. For L=O(-E), choose finitely many affine nonvanishing section charts of powers of L, equalize their degrees to n, and select finite R-algebra generators of each chart. Stacks28.27.11 section localization writes these generators as t/s_i^k. For one common K, use sections s_i^K and t s_i^(K-k) of L^(nK). Their projective chart ratios include every affine generator, hence give an immersion. Properness makes it a closed immersion. All these sections lie in R, since L^(nK) is a subsheaf of O. Their ideal J generates L^(nK), is proper because E is nonempty, and is unit off the marked point, hence primary. The projective map factors through the integral Rees blowup Bl_J(R). Its factor is a closed immersion containing the dense punctured open, so its defining ideal is zero. Thus Y=Bl_J(R). This proves the finite-list refinement actually used, not arbitrary-model cofinality.

Write the exceptional curves E_i, the pulled-back gauge divisor E_a=sum a_i E_i with a_i>0, and signed obstacle D=sum d_i E_i. Regular local factoriality makes the E_i actual effective Cartier divisors. Put Q_ij=deg_(E_i) O(E_j), with residue-field degrees included. Off-diagonal entries are nonnegative and symmetric: the effective zero divisors are computed by the same local intersection lengths. A nonzero section of a line bundle on any proper integral curve has nonnegative degree by its effective zero-divisor sequence. Every contracted integral curve is an E_i. Thus curve-nefness is Qz>=0.

For c_i=min(d_i,0), the feasible vectors z<=c, Qz>=0 contain the barrier b=-M a for sufficiently large M. The barrier is nef because the negative gauge divisor is globally generated. Coordinatewise maxima preserve the inequalities: for coordinate i keep an input's diagonal term and increase the nonnegative off-diagonal terms. In the compact box b<=z<=c, maximize each coordinate and take the finite coordinatewise maximum of those maximizers. This gives z* dominating the box. Every feasible z has max(z,b) in the box, so z* dominates ALL feasible vectors. Z*=sum z_i*E_i is ACTUAL negative effective real Cartier on ACTUAL Y, with degree >=0 on EVERY contracted integral curve. Its evaluation is in the geometric core and below f_D on EVERY support.

For ANY rational primary competitor q=-v(I)/s<=f_D let F_I=sum ord_(E_i)(I) E_i. Normal height-one intersection shows every ideal generator is a global section of O(-F_I); at the generic point of each E_i one generator attains the minimum and induces a nonzero section on that CURVE. Consequently A=-F_I/s is curve-nef, nonpositive, and divisorial tests ord_(E_i)/a_i give A_i<=d_i. Thus A<=Z*. On EVERY support p, use the valuation ring of Frac(R/p), not a homomorphism from Frac(R). Its generic centre is outside the exceptional fibre, properness gives a centre on Y, and the invertible exceptional lattice has a nonzero generic trivialization. Dividing each ideal generator by its local lattice generator is regular, proving q<=f_A<=f_(Z*); killed generators have infinite value and cause no exception. The raw rational-competitor identity then proves p(f_D)=f_(Z*).

Signed primary model obstacles are uniformly dense: their rational difference lattice obeys min(vI-vJ,vK-vH)=v(IH+KJ)-v(JH), contains constants through a, and separates all semivaluations using (g)+a^N, including different supports. Compact lattice Stone-Weierstrass and the raw Lipschitz bound give CE for EVERY continuous signed obstacle on EVERY such normal surface, arbitrary residue field and equal or mixed characteristic. Every canonical degree converges uniformly. Rational coefficient linear programming does not prove ideal attainment, semiampleness, finite generation, or a general O(1/m) rate.

For the characteristic-zero smooth theorem used later, the published BFJ setting is ONLY a smooth affine CLOSED germ over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field, dimension>=2; DVR and empty cases are direct. For a signed model F=F composed with a fixed retraction, adjoin a negative constant barrier to the max-directed family of nef coefficients below F. Weak closedness gives finite nef W. BFJ3.11 gives its substantive CLOSED-simplex continuous function H, and its ALL-retraction infimum. Divisorial density and refinements of the fixed model show H<=F on EVERY support. G331's exact BFJ D comparison shows every D competitor is below H. The canonical ideals are L-infinity(mW): to extend their divisorial tests to every support, truncate (g)+mhat^N with N>=m max(0,-min F), use closed-simplex continuity and cofinal retractions, and then v(g)>=v((g)+mhat^N). G331 contracts these primary ideals exactly to the local ring.

If W=0, H=0. Otherwise BFJ3.14 makes H strictly negative and thinness is bounded on the FIXED compact complex, so A_thin<=-CW there. The complete3.18 proof gives W_t<=W<=(1-C/t)W_(t-C) for real t>C: part(i) applies to any positive real scalar multiple, and the defining thinness argument of(ii) applies to real t. Taking t=m+C gives (1+C/m)W<=W_m<=W. Closed simplices and ALL-retraction infima yield 0<=H-h_m<=C max(0,-min F)/m on EVERY support. Uniform primary approximation proves H in C. Uniform model density and Lipschitz then prove smooth CE for all finite continuous signed obstacles at exactly the published hypotheses. Hironaka smooth char-zero principalization, multiplier subadditivity, thinness and smooth Izumi remain disclosed deeper foundations, not positive/mixed-characteristic premises. The separately retained coefficient-field, quotient and root proofs are DATA; no enlargement of this BFJ application is needed here.

On a reduced excellent curve the normalization centres are DVRs, the regular conductor has finite value at every branch, and every boundary fibre is singleton. Actual real Cartier slopes have empty curve tests; semilocal gluing and G331 positive descent give all nonpositive functions. Hence the geometric envelope is min(f,0), equal to the ideal envelope. This does not identify the boundary cone with literal multibranch classical/CLD radial extensions; the mixed-zero obstruction remains. Nilpotents reduce away and dimension-zero reduction has empty boundary.

Evidence and limitations: all four current416 actual FINALs were physically read with ALL five fields, and all four distinct expanded proofs were separately read in bounded untruncated outputs. notes.summary: Full conductor-envelope equivalence when the entire normalized boundary is bijective; explicit radicial and primary-conductor criteria.
notes.detailedSummary: Proves singleton fibres on both finite and infinite conductor strata, order/isometric C and D descent, raw envelope transport and CE equivalence. Finite radicial reduced conductor quotients and zero-dimensional conductor quotients suffice. Actual downstairs canonical primary profiles give all-curve-positive approximants. Nonsingleton-fibre descent remains open.
notes.text:
New conductor theorem, relative to ENTIRE qualified G331 and own n1. Let R be excellent reduced local with finite normalization S and conductor c. Set X=V_a(R) and Xtilde=V_(aS)(S), using every closed normalization centre and EVERY semivaluation support. Suppose restriction on the conductor quotient boundaries is injective. More precisely, the boundary of (S/c)_red maps injectively to that of (R/c)_red, with the quotient of the extended gauge, omitting empty zero-dimensional sections. Then rho:Xtilde->X is a homeomorphism. Indeed G331 grants surjectivity and compact Hausdorff quotient topology. At finite conductor value every fibre is singleton. At infinite value its ENTIRE fibre is precisely the conductor-quotient restriction fibre. The assumed injectivity handles all those fibres. Compact bijectivity gives the homeomorphism. This is a sufficient condition, not an asserted necessity for radiciality of an algebraic conductor map.

Here are two algebraically checkable sufficient cases. First, if R/c has dimension zero, c contains a power of m, so every centred semivaluation has finite conductor value. No quotient boundary remains; multiple normalization centres are allowed. Second, let B=(R/c)_red and T=(S/c)_red. Assume each prime p of B has exactly one prime P of T above it, and the finite field extension Frac(T/P)/Frac(B/p) is purely inseparable (in characteristic zero this means equal). These are the usual finite radicial conditions, stated explicitly. The reduction map B->T is injective: nilpotence upstairs of an element of R/c is already nilpotence in its injected subring. For a quotient semivaluation with support p, any lift has support P, uniquely. After quotienting the supports, its value on any nonzero field element x is forced by w(x)=v(x^(p^e))/p^e when an appropriate power lies in the old field; in characteristic zero it is already the same field. This proves uniqueness on every support, not just generic valuations. Existence is G331 finite lifting. Thus the quotient boundary is injective. No global common Frobenius exponent, perfection, F-finiteness or characteristic-zero restriction is required for this uniqueness proof. We do not invent a real field valuation through a nonzero support.

Because EVERY rho-fibre is singleton, G331's FULL positive C and D descent implies order bijections rho*:C_R->C_S and rho*:D_R->D_S. On C this is an isometry, since rho is surjective; continuity in either direction follows from the homeomorphism. Thus, for ANY obstacle for which the raw supremum is interpreted pointwise, the completed order bijection gives p_S(rho*f)=rho*p_R(f). For finite continuous signed obstacles the raw suprema are finite by n1. The continuous-envelope property is EQUIVALENT on R and S: every continuous source obstacle is the pullback of a continuous target obstacle, and an envelope belongs to C on one side iff it does on the other. The descended continuous envelope is independently geometric by positive descent, not by an unsupported assertion that a pointwise supremum is positive.

The canonical degree-m ideals satisfy A_m^R(f)=A_m^S(rho*f) intersect R, directly from surjective restriction and ALL defining inequalities. Equality after extension to S is NOT asserted. When CE holds, n1 gives uniform convergence in EVERY downstairs canonical degree. Each such profile has an ACTUAL negative effective Cartier presentation -E_(A_m)/m on its ACTUAL primary blowup; its degree on EVERY contracted integral curve is positive by ampleness. Consequently the uniform geometric envelope has actual positive approximants on the required model system. A continuous envelope need not itself have a single-model determination. Neither a source O(1/m) bound nor source finite generation is automatically inherited through contraction; n3 establishes an explicit rate and failure of finite generation for a particular family by a different argument.

The exact primary-gauge cocycle commutes with rho since w(aS)=v(a). For a new gauge b, d(v)=v(b), source and target divide by the same bounded positive denominator. Canonical ideals remain unchanged when the obstacle is transported homogeneously. Completion follows G331 and n1. For decreasing continuous obstacles with continuous envelopes, the actual D rule of n1 transports as well, with partial bottom and bottom retained. This theorem supplies envelope descent only under the stated singleton-fibre criterion; it does not settle arbitrary nonnormal gluing along a positive-dimensional conductor quotient.

Consequences: any excellent reduced local germ whose conductor is primary has CE exactly when all of its normal local centres have CE. In particular, the dimension-two normal theorem of n1 gives CE for every such germ whose normal centres all have dimension at most two. Under the finite radicial conductor-quotient condition the same equivalence holds even when the infinite-conductor boundary is NONEMPTY. If S is a normal local surface it has CE in any equal/mixed characteristic by n1; if its centres are smooth affine closed germs over an algebraically closed characteristic-zero field it has CE in every dimension by n1. These are narrowed conclusions with explicit source hypotheses, not added premises for unrestricted ORIGINAL P12.3.

The point where the unrestricted descent problem remains is now precise: for a quotient boundary with nonsingleton fibres there is no automatic constancy of a source greatest minorant. This note neither takes a fibrewise minimum as psh nor asserts arbitrary finite-map envelope compatibility. Products, energy and full finite operators remain separate.

notes.summary: Nonisolated nonnormal CE in every dimension over algebraically closed characteristic zero; explicit all-characteristic cusp envelope error <=2/m and char-zero non-FG.
notes.detailedSummary: Numerical-semigroup cusps have identical reduced conductor quotients and a full boundary homeomorphism, including infinite-conductor supports. Smooth source CE gives all continuous signed obstacles in every dimension at exact hypotheses; surfaces work over all fields and Z_p cusp gives a mixed-characteristic case. A cancellation-sensitive ideal sequence proves 2/m all-support canonical error in every dimension/field. In char zero its envelope lies outside the entire finite real raw ideal cone and canonical finite generation fails.
notes.text:
New higher-dimensional nonnormal continuous-envelope sector and explicit quantitative example, using ENTIRE qualified G331 and own n1--n2. Let H be a proper numerical semigroup (a finitely generated additive subsemigroup of the nonnegative integers containing zero with finite complement) and let c be its conductor integer: every integer >=c belongs to H and c-1 does not. For any field k and d>=2, set R_H=k[t^h (h in H),z_1,...,z_(d-1)] localized at the origin, and S=k[t,z_1,...,z_(d-1)] localized there. Both rings are excellent finite-type domains of dimension d. S is finite over R_H since t is integral (some positive t^h lies downstairs), and their fraction fields coincide because gcd(H)=1. S is regular and integrally closed, hence is the normalization. There is just one centre over the origin. Its conductor is exactly t^c S. To verify this on polynomials, all terms of t-degree >=c multiply into the semigroup ring. If a polynomial has a term of degree h<c, multiply by t^(c-1-h); its coefficient of the forbidden degree c-1 remains nonzero. Distinct t-degrees cannot cancel it. Conductor commutes with localization because S/R_H is finite. The reduced conductor quotients are BOTH k[z_1,...,z_(d-1)] at the origin, and their map is the identity.

The infinite-conductor boundary is nonempty: a valuation killing t and centered on the z-ring belongs to it. Thus n2 proves a full boundary homeomorphism including an actual positive-dimensional-support conductor stratum. In characteristic zero over algebraically closed k, the exact smooth source theorem of n1 gives a greatest continuous independently geometric C/D envelope for EVERY finite continuous signed obstacle on EVERY R_H, in EVERY dimension d. Uniform convergence holds in every canonical degree and for every primary gauge. These are nonnormal nonisolated germs: the normalization fails along t=0, a locus of dimension d-1, because t remains integral but missing at its generic point. The result goes beyond normal smooth finite quotients; it is not inferred from characteristic-zero resolution of these singular germs.

For d=2 the source is a normal surface, so the same all-continuous-obstacle theorem holds over EVERY field, including imperfect fields and positive characteristic. There is also a mixed-characteristic example R=Z_p[[t^2,t^3]]=Z_p[[a,b]]/(b^2-a^3), S=Z_p[[t]]. Grouping even/odd powers proves the indicated embedding and finiteness; S is complete regular of dimension two, its fraction field agrees, and t^2 S is the conductor. The reduced conductor quotients are both Z_p. They have a nonempty centred boundary (the p-order ray), so infinite-conductor supports have not been discarded. N2 plus the normal-surface theorem proves CE for EVERY continuous signed obstacle here. Higher-dimensional positive/mixed-characteristic smooth source CE remains unproved by this argument.

For H=<2,3> there is a new explicit all-support example in EVERY dimension d>=2 and EVERY field, independent of any general source CE theorem. Use gauge a=(t^2,t^3,z_1,...,z_(d-1)), b=z_1+t and J=(b,t^2,z_2,...,z_(d-1)) in S. J is primary. By the homeomorphism define the continuous downstairs A(v)=w(J), where rho(w)=v, and obstacle f=-A. For integers m>=1 form the ACTUAL downstairs primary ideal
K_m=(b^m(z_1-mt), t^2 b^m, t^(2m+2))+(z_2,...,z_(d-1))^m.
When d=2 omit the last summand and put U=+infinity below. The first generator has no t-linear coefficient: m z_1^m-m z_1^m=0, including in characteristic dividing m. All its other t-degrees are zero or >=2, so it lies in R. The remaining generators lie there too. The radical contains t^2,t^3,z_1 and all the other z_j, hence K_m is proper primary. No generator is treated as a supplied executable expression.

Here is the universal bound, including EVERY support and infinite coordinate. Write s=w(t), u=w(z_1), B=w(b), U=min_(j>=2)w(z_j), so min(2s,u,U)=1 and A=min(B,2s,U). A is finite. Every displayed generator has value >=mA, hence w(K_m)>=mA. If U=A, the added ideal has value mU=mA, giving equality. Otherwise A<U. If 2s<=B, then s is finite and u=s: unequal values would force B=min(s,u)<2s. Since U>2s and min(2s,s,U)=1, s=u=1. The last original generator then has value mA+2. In the remaining case B<2s, A=B<U. If s<=u, then s is finite; B>=s. If s>1 all of 2s,u,U would exceed one, a contradiction. Thus s<=1, and t^2 b^m has value mA+2s<=mA+2. If s>u (including s=infinity), B=w(z_1-mt)=u: for m nonzero in k, m is a unit and the values are unequal, and if m=0 in k the second expression is simply z_1. The normalization and U>u give u=1, so the first generator has value mA+1. These cases exhaust all possibilities, including B=infinity, U=infinity, killed coordinates and cancellation. Consequently
0<=v(K_m)/m-A(v)<=2/m on the ENTIRE normalized boundary.

Therefore f is a uniform limit from below of -v(K_m)/m. Each profile is the evaluation of ACTUAL -E_(K_m)/m on ACTUAL Bl_(K_m)(R), negative effective and relatively ample, with positive degree on EVERY contracted integral curve. Thus f belongs to independently geometric C even in higher positive characteristic where general CE is unknown. It is its own greatest C/D minorant. Since K_m subset A_m^R(f), the canonical profiles themselves obey the EVERY-degree uniform estimate 0<=p(f)-h_m^R(f)<=2/m. This establishes a quantitative geometric envelope across the infinite-conductor stratum without a conductor-value/N error or a root-map assumption.

In characteristic ZERO f is outside the ENTIRE finite REAL raw negative ideal cone Q_R, and its canonical algebra is NOT finitely generated. Define w_infinity by killing t,z_2,... and giving z_1 value one; define w_star by killing z_2,... and using monomial weights (t,b)=(1,2), with z_1=b-t. Both satisfy the chosen gauge, and A(w_infinity)=1, A(w_star)=2. For ANY proper primary downstairs ideal I, its image after killing the other z_j is primary in k[t^2,t^3,z_1]. Let e=w_infinity(I)>0. A generator attaining e has a unit denominator at both valuations. Its formal expansion has no t-degree-one terms, has nonzero z_1^e coefficient, and has zero t z_1^(e-1) coefficient. Its total-degree-e homogeneous part therefore cannot be a scalar multiple of b^e in characteristic zero. After z_1=b-t it contains some t^(e-j)b^j with j<e, of w_star-value e+j<=2e-1. Other total degrees cannot cancel this monomial. Thus w_star(I)<2w_infinity(I). Every nonzero finite nonnegative REAL combination of proper primary gauges preserves this strict inequality; unit terms vanish. A has equality, so A is outside the raw positive cone and f outside Q_R. Finite homogeneous generation of the canonical algebra would force a rational primary envelope by the elementary argument in n1, contradicting this separation. No claim of non-finite-generation in positive characteristic follows from the characteristic-zero argument.

This is continuous-envelope regularity WITH a canonical O(1/m) bound and WITHOUT canonical finite generation for an explicit cancellation-sensitive nonnormal higher-dimensional example. It is not a counterexample to CE, nor a raw geometric-core attainment claim. Under another gauge the same homogeneously transported obstacle keeps all canonical ideals, and the bound is divided by min v(new gauge)>0. G331's literal radial scope distinction, curve min(f,0), nilpotent reduction and empty dimension-zero case remain unchanged.

notes.summary: Explicit actual-primary threefold obstruction: generic sections on exceptional surfaces do not imply all-curve-nef divisorial parts.
notes.detailedSummary: On the blowup of a regular threefold origin and two rational exceptional points, I=(z)+m^2 has divisorial part E1+2E2+2E3. Its negative restricts to H-eP-eQ on Bl_2(P^2), with degree -1 on the joining line. The model is proved an actual primary blowup. Every-support domination survives, but the surface nefness inference fails. This is not a CE counterexample.
notes.text:
Precise THREE-dimensional obstruction to the surface competitor method; this is NOT a continuous-envelope counterexample. Support: ENTIRE qualified G331 and own n1 for the finite section/ACTUAL primary presentation argument. Let R=k[x,y,z]_(x,y,z) for ANY field k, m=(x,y,z), and I=(z)+m^2, a proper primary ideal. Blow up the origin, with exceptional E_0=P^2_k. Blow up the two distinct k-rational points P=[1:0:0], Q=[0:1:0] of E_0. Their disjoint point ideals can be blown up at once; equivalently do the two point blowups successively. All charts are regular (ordinary point blowups in regular coordinates). Let Y be the result, E_1 the strict transform of E_0, and E_2,E_3 the new exceptional planes. Then E_1=Bl_(P,Q)(P^2), while E_2,E_3 are disjoint copies of P^2.

This explicit Y is an ACTUAL primary model. Its second-stage negative tautological bundle O(-E_2-E_3) is relatively ample for Y->Bl_m(R); this is the blowup of the disjoint union of the two point ideals, invertible/unit on the complement. The first negative tautological bundle O(-E_0) is ample. The COMPLETE immediately read Stacks29.38.7--8 gives, for an integer a sufficiently large, O(-E_2-E_3-a pullback(E_0)) ample over R. Here pullback(E_0)=E_1+E_2+E_3. Thus E=aE_1+(a+1)E_2+(a+1)E_3 is ACTUAL effective Cartier, full exceptional support, and O(-E) relatively ample. Stacks37.53.6 gives H^0(Y,O)=R. The finite affine-section localization/projective immersion/Rees argument proved in n1 applies verbatim in this dimension to THIS explicit Y: it requires normal target, ample negative exceptional bundle and projectivity, not surface resolution. A finite set of sections of O(-nE) gives a proper primary J and identifies Y with Bl_J(R). This is an explicit construction and no cofinality assertion for arbitrary threefold modifications.

The divisorial part of I on Y is F_I=E_1+2E_2+2E_3. The order at E_0 is one, realized by z. In the x-chart of the first blowup, with v=y/x and w=z/x, I O=x(w,x). At P the regular local parameters are x,v,w. Thus the residual ideal (w,x) has point order one, so the second exceptional order is two. The y-chart gives the identical calculation at Q. The strict E_1 order remains one. All ideal generators are global sections of O(-F_I) by normal height-one intersection, and at the generic point of EACH E_i at least one realizes the minimum and restricts to a nonzero section, exactly as in the surface competitor proof.

Nevertheless A=-F_I fails the mandatory contracted-curve positivity test. On E_1 let H be the pullback of a line in P^2 and e_P,e_Q its two exceptional curves.
